stories.dek: With about half an hour of trading left the S&P 500 is 7,707.82, down 0.73%, and the Nasdaq is down 1.08%. Two things did it. The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years reached 5.11%, up from 4.97% on Tuesday, after this morning's business survey came in far stronger than expected at 58.4 — which makes a rate cut less likely, not more. And oil jumped again, Brent at $98.40. For someone holding good businesses for years, higher rates mostly cut the price people will pay for future profits rather than the profits themselves. The closing bell is next.
stories.headline: Higher borrowing costs and dearer oil pull American shares lower
stories.short: Rates and oil push US shares lower into the close

stories.dek: The VIX, the market's fear gauge, is 15.06, up 5.97% on Tuesday's 14.21 close. It has spent this whole week under 15, which the BuyTrigger ladder calls the calm band; 15 to 20 is the normal band, the second rung. It touched 15.45 earlier and has faded back since, so it is sitting almost exactly on the line. For a family investor the gauge matters only as a signal of when shares go on sale, and the system's buy window does not open until 30. The closing print, not this one, sets tonight's band.
stories.headline: The fear gauge nudges above 15 for the first time this week
stories.short: Fear gauge sits just above 15, out of the calm band

stories.dek: Oil ran a second time this afternoon. US crude is $92.54, up 2.23%, and Brent, the international grade, is $98.40, up 3.13% and $1.60 short of $100. Two hours ago US crude was up only 0.72% against Brent's 2.12%, and I read that gap as evidence the problem was seaborne — Libya's shut pipeline and tight diesel. That reading did not hold: the gap between the two grades has closed to $5.86 from $6.26, so the buying is in both. For long-term holders, dearer oil feeds back into the inflation figures that set interest rates. Tonight's settlement is the test.
stories.headline: Oil jumps again and American crude finally catches up with Brent
stories.short: Oil runs again; US crude closes the gap to Brent

claims.claim: Daily change in the mortgage rate
Last date the rate was higher

stories.dek: The US 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose 9 basis points today to 7.26%, matching the high set in early 2025 and the highest since May 2024. This is the same move that took the government's ten-year borrowing rate to 5.11%, arriving at a kitchen table rather than on a screen — mortgage rates track that yield closely. For a family investor it is the clearest read on what tighter money actually costs households, and it works through homebuilders, banks and consumer spending over months rather than days. Watch whether it holds above 7.25% into next week.
stories.headline: American mortgage rates hit their highest level since May 2024
stories.short: US mortgage rate 7.26%, highest since May 2024

stories.dek: Robinhood is $123.95, down 0.24%, having been up 0.53% two hours ago and up 1.40% at lunchtime. It had been the one watchlist name holding green on a falling market through two straight editions, and it has now turned — with no company news behind it in either direction. Its low today was $122.55, so it faded rather than broke. For someone holding for years the point is that nothing about the business changed today, only the price and the mood around it. The closing print is worth noting either way.
stories.headline: Robinhood ($HOOD) gives way late after holding up all afternoon
stories.short: Robinhood turns red late with no company news

claims.claim: Edgewater Research channel-check note on stalled market-share growth

stories.dek: AppLovin is $315.79, down 3.94%, after trading as low as $304.77 — it has recovered $11.02 from that low, against $6.08 two hours ago. The whole two-day fall traces to a single research note from Edgewater arguing its market-share growth has stalled, and no firm has actually changed a rating on the stock. Its ad-tech peers fell alongside it earlier today. For a family investor this is a live example of a sector repricing on an opinion rather than on anything the company disclosed. Watch for a real rating action after the close.
stories.headline: AppLovin ($APP) claws back losses with still no analyst downgrade
stories.short: AppLovin recovers $11 off its low, still unrated

stories.dek: Nvidia is $225.31, down 1.56%, having been down 1.85% two hours ago. Across the market the Nasdaq now trails the S&P 500 by 0.35 percentage points, narrowed from 0.49 at 18:30. That gap is the clearest single measure of how much rising interest rates are hurting technology in particular: the more of a company's worth sits in profits far in the future, the more a higher borrowing rate takes off it today. It narrowed this afternoon even while oil ran, which is not what a pure rate shock looks like. The close settles it.
stories.headline: Technology shares claw back ground in the final hour of trading
stories.short: Tech recovers late; Nasdaq gap to S&P narrows
